title: 5 Things You’re Doing That Look Right But Aren’t
paragraphs: 5 Things You’re Doing That Look Right But Aren’t
Some sins don’t walk in wearing black.

They come dressed like discipline.
Like leadership.
Like “wisdom.”
Like being “careful.”
And that is exactly why they’re dangerous.
Here are 5 things you may be doing that look right… but aren’t:

1. Serving in public while neglecting God in private
You post the verse.
You lead the group.
You show up for ministry.
But your prayer life is cold, your Bible stays closed, and your heart is running on fumes.
That is not strength. That is slow spiritual starvation.
Jesus warned about outward righteousness with inward emptiness.
“These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me” (Matthew 15:8).

2. Calling fear “discernment”
Not every delay is wisdom.
Not every hesitation is the Holy Spirit.
Sometimes we say “I’m just waiting on God” when the truth is we are terrified to obey.
Discernment listens.
Fear stalls.
There is a difference.

3. Using truth without love
Yes, truth matters. Deeply.
But some people are not defending holiness. They are just hiding cruelty behind Bible words.
If your correction has no tears, no humility, no gentleness, it may be more flesh than faith.
Truth without love becomes a weapon.
And Jesus never used truth to crush repentant people.

4. Looking holy while feeding pride
You stopped the obvious sin.
Good.
But now pride has taken the throne.
You compare.
You secretly feel superior.
You thank God you are “not like them.”
That is still darkness—just dressed in church clothes.
The Pharisee looked clean.
The tax collector went home justified.

5. Protecting your image instead of confessing your sin
You want to appear strong.
Untouchable.
Mature.
But hidden sin grows in silence.
Healing begins where honesty begins.
What we conceal, sin deepens.
What we confess, grace can reach.
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us” (1 John 1:9).

God is not exposing you to shame you.
He is confronting you to save you.

Jesus did not die only for the sins that looked ugly.
He died for the ones that looked respectable too.

For the polished pride.
The religious mask.
The clean-looking compromise.
The fear called wisdom.
The performance called faith.

This is the Gospel:
You do not have to keep pretending.
You can repent.
You can come into the light.
And in Christ, there is mercy for even the mess that hides behind “rightness.”

So ask yourself:
What in my life looks spiritual… but is actually keeping me from Jesus?

Let it search you.
Let it break you.
Then let Christ heal what religion taught you to hide.
